subject: Biotechnology
title: Viral Vector Vaccines
description: A quick, practical guide to Viral Vector Vaccines.

hook.text: Use a harmless virus to carry genes from a dangerous one — the body mounts a defense without facing the real threat.

buildup.text: AstraZeneca's COVID vaccine uses a chimpanzee adenovirus carrying the spike gene — the vector cannot replicate.

discovery.text: J&J used human adenovirus 26 — a single dose induced strong immunity because the vector triggers innate responses too.

twist.text: Pre-existing immunity to the vector can blunt the vaccine — people who had that adenovirus before respond less.

climax.text: The Ebola vaccine rVSV-ZEBOV uses a livestock virus carrying Ebola glycoprotein — 100% effective in ring vaccination trials.

punchline.text: A tame virus carrying enemy intel — viral vectors train immunity safely.

quiz.question: What is a challenge of using human adenovirus as a vaccine vector?
options: Human adenoviruses are too large to carry vaccine genes
Pre-existing immunity to the vector can reduce vaccine effectiveness
Adenoviruses always integrate into the genome permanently

details.summary: Viral vector vaccines use harmless modified viruses to deliver genetic instructions for making target antigens, triggering strong immune responses without causing disease. Adenoviral vectors powered the Oxford-AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccines reaching billions of people.
details.whyItMatters: Viral vector vaccines combine the strong immunogenicity of live vaccines with modern safety engineering. Their success against COVID-19 proved the platform at unprecedented scale and opened doors for vaccines against HIV, malaria, and Ebola.
takeaways: Viral vectors deliver antigen genes using harmless modified viruses
Adenoviral vectors were used in two major COVID-19 vaccines
Pre-existing immunity to common vectors can reduce vaccine effectiveness

faq.question: Can viral vector vaccines cause infection with the vector virus?
faq.answer: No. Vaccine vectors are replication-deficient, meaning essential genes are deleted so the virus enters cells and delivers its payload but cannot replicate or spread. The vector delivers the antigen gene then is cleared by the immune system without causing disease.

faq.question: Why is pre-existing immunity a problem for viral vectors?
faq.answer: Many people have antibodies against common adenoviruses from prior natural infections. These antibodies can neutralize the vaccine vector before it delivers its payload, reducing effectiveness. Using rare human serotypes or chimpanzee adenoviruses overcomes this problem.
